author: ribeye
dek: A Youngstown man watched Minnesota flood on the news and spent the rest of the weekend flood-proofing a basement that has never once flooded.
disclaimer: Parody: the DeAngelo family of Youngstown is fictional. The Minnesota flooding is real, as reported by FOX 9 in September 2026.
headline: Youngstown Man Watches Minnesota Flood, Immediately Flood-Proofs a Basement That Has Never Flooded

ohio_quotes.quote: Minnesota got six inches of rain in one day. Six. I timed our sump pump with a kitchen timer and a bucket, and I did not like what I found.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Ray DeAngelo, Youngstown

ohio_quotes.quote: He moved the deep freezer, the Christmas bins, and his father's entire Youngstown Sheet and Tube collection upstairs. The man flood-proofed the basement and flooded the living room with stuff.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Tina DeAngelo, Youngstown

ohio_story: YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio — Ray DeAngelo has lived in the same house off Belmont Avenue for 31 years, and in all that time his basement has never taken on a drop of water. That perfect record ended as a concern, if not as a fact, on Saturday, when Ray watched the news out of Minnesota and decided his basement's luck had officially run out.

"Six inches in a day," Ray said, standing in his driveway in a Youngstown State Penguins sweatshirt, a brand-new second sump pump still in the box at his feet. "I watched them evacuate a whole nursing home in a pontoon boat. A pontoon boat, Tina. We don't even own a pontoon boat." By noon he had moved the deep freezer, three bins of Christmas decorations, and his late father's Youngstown Sheet and Tube memorabilia up the basement stairs, bought two tarps and a pallet of sandbags at the store on Belmont, and drawn up what he calls "the plan" on the back of a Canfield Fair flyer. His daughter, home from YSU for the weekend, was put in charge of holding the flashlight.

Tina, meanwhile, has taken a more measured view. "The basement is dry, the sump pump works, and the only water down there is the dehumidifier doing its job," she said, surveying a living room now occupied by a deep freezer and a cardboard box labeled MILL STUFF — DO NOT THROW OUT. "But he is happy, the Buckeyes won, and nobody got hurt, so I am letting him have this one." Ray says phase two of the plan — a third sump pump, "just in case" — begins next weekend, right after the Friday night game at Stambaugh Stadium. The freezer, he notes, stays upstairs until further notice.
real_summary: A line of thunderstorms formed late Friday, Sept. 18, 2026, and repeatedly passed over the same communities in south and southeastern Minnesota into early Saturday, Sept. 19. About 700 square miles across the region received six inches or more of rain within 24 hours, according to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. The storm was assessed as at least as destructive as the July 2026 mega-rain that had struck many of the same communities just months earlier.

In New Richland, a town of about 1,200 people in Waseca County, more than three-quarters of homes were damaged by the flooding. The New Richland Care Center, a skilled nursing facility, had to be evacuated with help from a neighbor with a pontoon boat, high school students, and first responders; 36 residents were relocated to other senior care communities. City officials expected 10 to 12 homes in New Richland to be declared total losses.

Standing water remained in pockets about six inches deep days after the storm, and saturated soil kept forcing water into basements; officials warned residents not to pump basements out too quickly, for fear the walls could collapse. The care center sustained damage up to four feet high that will need to be gutted, with officials hoping to reopen it in six to 12 months. Gov. Tim Walz requested federal disaster assistance for the period of Sept. 18 to Sept. 20, 2026, covering Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca counties.
source_note: FOX 9 reporting, Sep. 24, 2026: New Richland flooding aftermath; 80% of homes impacted; care center evacuation; 10 to 12 homes likely total losses.
